blocks.path: Overview - Coronary heart disease
s: Coronary heart disease (CHD) is a major cause of death in the UK and worldwide.
CHD is sometimes called ischaemic heart disease or coronary artery disease.

blocks.path: Overview - Coronary heart disease > Symptoms of coronary heart disease (CHD)
s: The main symptoms of coronary heart disease are:

blocks.path: Overview - Coronary heart disease > Symptoms of coronary heart disease (CHD)
s: chest pain (angina)

blocks.path: Overview - Coronary heart disease > Symptoms of coronary heart disease (CHD)
s: shortness of breath

blocks.path: Overview - Coronary heart disease > Symptoms of coronary heart disease (CHD)
s: pain in your neck, shoulders, jaw or arms

blocks.path: Overview - Coronary heart disease > Symptoms of coronary heart disease (CHD)
s: feeling faint

blocks.path: Overview - Coronary heart disease > Symptoms of coronary heart disease (CHD)
s: feeling sick (nausea)

blocks.path: Overview - Coronary heart disease > Symptoms of coronary heart disease (CHD)
s: But not everyone has the same symptoms and some people may not have any before coronary heart disease is diagnosed.

blocks.path: Overview - Coronary heart disease > Causes of coronary heart disease (CHD)
s: Coronary heart disease is the term that describes what happens when your heart's blood supply is blocked or interrupted by a build-up of fatty substances in the coronary arteries.

blocks.path: Overview - Coronary heart disease > Causes of coronary heart disease (CHD)
s: Over time, the walls of your arteries can become furred up with fatty deposits.
This process is known as atherosclerosis and the fatty deposits are called atheroma.

blocks.path: Overview - Coronary heart disease > Causes of coronary heart disease (CHD)
s: Atherosclerosis can be caused by lifestyle factors, such as smoking and regularly drinking excessive amounts of alcohol.

blocks.path: Overview - Coronary heart disease > Causes of coronary heart disease (CHD)
s: You're also more at risk of getting atherosclerosis if you have conditions like high cholesterol, high blood pressure (hypertension) or diabetes.

blocks.path: Overview - Coronary heart disease > Diagnosing coronary heart disease (CHD)
s: If a doctor feels you're at risk of coronary heart disease, they may carry out a risk assessment.

blocks.path: Overview - Coronary heart disease > Diagnosing coronary heart disease (CHD)
s: They'll ask you about your medical and family history and your lifestyle, and they'll take a blood test.

blocks.path: Overview - Coronary heart disease > Diagnosing coronary heart disease (CHD)
s: Further tests may be needed to confirm coronary heart disease, including:

blocks.path: Overview - Coronary heart disease > Diagnosing coronary heart disease (CHD)
s: electrocardiogram (ECG)

blocks.path: Overview - Coronary heart disease > Diagnosing coronary heart disease (CHD)
s: echocardiogram

blocks.path: Overview - Coronary heart disease > Diagnosing coronary heart disease (CHD)
s: chest x-ray

blocks.path: Overview - Coronary heart disease > Diagnosing coronary heart disease (CHD)
s: coronary angiogram

blocks.path: Overview - Coronary heart disease > Diagnosing coronary heart disease (CHD)
s: Read more about how coronary heart disease is diagnosed.

blocks.path: Overview - Coronary heart disease > Treating coronary heart disease (CHD)
s: Coronary heart disease cannot be cured but treatment can help manage the symptoms and reduce the chances of problems such as heart attacks.

blocks.path: Overview - Coronary heart disease > Treating coronary heart disease (CHD)
s: Treatment can include:

blocks.path: Overview - Coronary heart disease > Treating coronary heart disease (CHD)
s: lifestyle changes, such as regular exercise and stopping smoking

blocks.path: Overview - Coronary heart disease > Treating coronary heart disease (CHD)
s: medicines

blocks.path: Overview - Coronary heart disease > Treating coronary heart disease (CHD)
s: angioplasty – where balloons and stents are used to treat narrow heart arteries

blocks.path: Overview - Coronary heart disease > Treating coronary heart disease (CHD)
s: surgery

blocks.path: Overview - Coronary heart disease > Recovering from the effects of coronary heart disease (CHD)
s: If you've had a heart attack, an angioplasty, or heart surgery, you’ll want to get back to as full a life as possible.

blocks.path: Overview - Coronary heart disease > Recovering from the effects of coronary heart disease (CHD)
s: Advice and support is available to help you deal with aspects of your life that may have been affected by coronary heart disease.

blocks.path: Overview - Coronary heart disease > Recovering from the effects of coronary heart disease (CHD)
s: Read more about recovering from the effects of coronary heart disease.

blocks.path: Overview - Coronary heart disease > Preventing coronary heart disease (CHD)
s: You can reduce your risk of getting coronary heart disease by making some simple lifestyle changes.

blocks.path: Overview - Coronary heart disease > Preventing coronary heart disease (CHD)
s: These include:

blocks.path: Overview - Coronary heart disease > Preventing coronary heart disease (CHD)
s: eating a healthy, balanced diet

blocks.path: Overview - Coronary heart disease > Preventing coronary heart disease (CHD)
s: being physically active

blocks.path: Overview - Coronary heart disease > Preventing coronary heart disease (CHD)
s: giving up smoking

blocks.path: Overview - Coronary heart disease > Preventing coronary heart disease (CHD)
s: controlling blood cholesterol and sugar levels

blocks.path: Overview - Coronary heart disease > Preventing coronary heart disease (CHD)
s: Keeping your heart healthy will also have other health benefits, such as helping reduce your risk of stroke and dementia.

blocks.path: Overview - Coronary heart disease > The heart
s: The heart is a muscle about the size of your fist.
It pumps blood around your body and beats approximately 70 times a minute.

blocks.path: Overview - Coronary heart disease > The heart
s: After the blood leaves the right side of the heart, it goes to your lungs where it picks up oxygen.

blocks.path: Overview - Coronary heart disease > The heart
s: The oxygen-rich blood returns to your heart and is then pumped to the body's organs through a network of arteries.

blocks.path: Overview - Coronary heart disease > The heart
s: The blood returns to your heart through veins before being pumped back to your lungs again.
This process is called circulation.

blocks.path: Overview - Coronary heart disease > The heart
s: The heart gets its own supply of blood from a network of blood vessels on the heart's surface called coronary arteries.

s: This video shows how your heart works and what happens when your coronary arteries stop functioning properly.
